Sup A: seidel_2018_detailed_kinetic_model · Kinetic modeling of methanol synthesis from renewable resources (Detailed kinetic model)
The detailed kinetic model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide over a commercial copper/zinc oxide/alumina catalyst. It predicts the rates of CO hydrogenation, CO₂ hydrogenation, and the reverse water-gas shift reaction from gas partial pressures and temperature. It uses a Langmuir–Hinshelwood framework built from elementary surface steps, with fast steps treated as quasi-equilibrated. The detailed kinetic formulation is steady-state and algebraic, rather than a dynamic model with evolving states. Its parameters were fitted to 140 steady-state experiments in a differential Micro-Berty reactor and its predictions were compared with those measurements; dynamic switching experiments in the paper were used for a separate model extension. The authors present the kinetics as a basis for modelling methanol reactors handling changing feed compositions, including for chemical energy storage.

Sup B: seidel_2018_simplified_kinetic_model_dynamic · Kinetic modeling of methanol synthesis from renewable resources (Simplified kinetic model, dynamic φ)
This model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide over a commercial copper/zinc oxide/alumina catalyst in a differential CSTR. It predicts gas composition and methanol production while tracking changes in the fraction of reduced catalyst surface centers, which affect the activity of the different reactions. The simplified model combines lumped Langmuir–Hinshelwood rate expressions and algebraic surface coverages with dynamic balances for the catalyst and reactor. It was fitted and tested against 140 steady-state experiments and feed-switching experiments reported by Vollbrecht (2007), using global optimization. The dynamic version reproduced the transient experiments better than a version with quasi-static catalyst states, and the simplified model fitted steady-state data almost as well as the detailed model while improving identifiability. The authors propose it for dynamic simulation and future design and control of methanol reactors for chemical energy storage under changing feed conditions; a 2020 corrigendum clarified the equations used.

answer.description: A and B model methanol synthesis from CO, CO₂, and hydrogen over the same Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃ catalyst, including CO and CO₂ hydrogenation and reverse water-gas shift. Both were fitted to the same 140 steady-state experiments and are intended for changing feed conditions. A is a detailed, steady-state algebraic Langmuir–Hinshelwood model based on elementary surface steps; B uses lumped kinetics and adds dynamic balances for reactor gas composition and the changing fraction of reduced catalyst centers. B also captures feed-switching transients and improves identifiability relative to A.
